posts.cooked: double sleeved? I've not heard of anyone doing that before. Does that mean you put the card in a sleeve and then put the sleeved card in another sleeve? Why?

posts.name: Reckless
posts.cooked:
arenson9:

double sleeved? I've not heard of anyone doing that before. Does that mean you put the card in a sleeve and then put the sleeved card in another sleeve? Why?

There are smaller, delicate sleeves that are built to fit inside of a regular sleeve.  The idea is that you can sleeve a card in one of these smaller sleeves upside down then sleeve it with a regular sleeve as normal so that it is better protected from wear.  I had a friend who (foolishly, in my opinion) played with his Magic: The Gathering cards after he was thoroughly intoxicated on his 21st birthday. 

I'd rather avoid any grisly details…suffice it to say those sleeves were a big help.

posts.name: tzgardner
posts.cooked:
Sure.  The zip file attached has the stl files if you want to print them out.  The skp files are Google Sketchup files if you want to alter them to fit your needs.

 

For the damage tokens: 

Downloaded the font RedStatebluestate BB (I think that was from Spiff's site)

Just printed them on a regular piece of paper with background color rectangles the size of the tokens.

Cut them out and ran them through a sticker maker.

When I got the extra token pack, I was able to cut out of the left over cardboard material about 10 token sized pieces.

Then just stuck my printouts to the cardboard.

 

They work great for Omnitron and Legacy to remember what damage type they are immune to.
